questions.question: One rupee note in India bears the signature of _________ .

options.text: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
The Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

questions.solution: One rupee note in India bears the signature of Finance Secretary while other currency notes in India bear the signature of RBI governor.

questions.question: How is the poverty line calculated in India?
questions.solution:
• The poverty line estimate in India is solely based on calorie intake of food.
 
• A person is said to be above poverty line if he/she has enough money to buy 2100 calories per day living in Urban area or 2400 calorie per day living in rural area.
 
• The poverty line is calculated every 5 years.

questions.question: In which Five-Year-Plan the poverty eradication was mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__5__th__ Five Year Plan__**

 
• The Fifth(5th) Five-Year Plan focused on **poverty eradication (Garibi Hatao), employment, and justice.**
 
• Fifth Five Year Plan duration was **1974 to 1978**.
 
• In this plan, the priority was given to the **agriculture sector**, and then to the **industry and mines**.
 
• Overall this plan was a success which gained a **growth of 4.8% against the target of 4.4%.**
 
• The **draft of this plan** was created and released by the **D.P. Dhar**. This plan was **put to an end in 1978**.
 
• **Rolling Plan**: This plan was introduced with an annual plan for **1978-79 **and as an extension of the terminated **fifth-five year plan**.

questions.question: Which countries’ currency is often “hard currency”?
questions.solution:
• Hard currencies is issued by developed countries that have a strong industrial economy accompanied by a stable government.
 
• Some of the most common hard currencies include U.K. pound sterling (GBP), Euro (EUR) and U.S. dollar (USD).
 
• Hard currencies remain relatively stable and experiences only minor short-term fluctuations in the foreign exchange market.

questions.question: How many times generally a Bill is read in Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Thrice**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• A Bill is generally read thrice in the parliament.
 
• The first reading of the bill takes place when it is introduced to a legislature.
 
• During the second reading, the draft of the bill is read.
 
• During the third reading, the bill is read with all amendments and given final approval by a legislative body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__There are 4 types of Bills which can be introduced in the Parliament__

 
• Ordinary Bills - Related to any matter apart from financial subjects.
 
• Money Bills - Related to financial matters like taxation.
 
• Financial Bills - Related to financial matters other than those things included in Money bills
 
• Constitution amendment bills - Related to the amendment of the Constitution.

__Ordinary Bill:-__

__
 
• It can be introduced either in the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
 
• It can be introduced either by a minister or by a private member.
 
• It is introduced without the recommendation of the president.
 
• It can be amended or rejected by the Rajya Sabha.__
 
• It can be detained by the Rajya Sabha for a maximum period of six months.
 
• It does not require the certification of the Speaker when transmitted to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Its defeat in the Lok Sabha may lead to the resignation of the government.
 
• It can be rejected, approved, or returned for reconsideration by the President.

__There are five stages in the enactment of an ordinary bill __

 
• **First reading** ( in the House in which it is introduced)
 
• **Second reading** ( in the House in which it is introduced)
 
• **Third reading **( in the House in which it is introduced)
 
• Bill in the second House ( first reading, second reading, third reading )
 
• Assent of the President.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a good example of sharing power among different social groups?

options.text: None of the option is correct

questions.solution:
• A community government is one in which different social groups are given the power to handle the affairs related to their communities.
 
• The community government was first originated in Belgium.
 
• Community government has the power regarding cultural educational and language related issues.

questions.question: Who conducts the work of the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
• The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The Deputy Chairman is elected internally by the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, who presides over its sessions.

questions.question: The Concept of Public Interest Litigation was originated in which country?
questions.solution:
• The term Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was originated in the United States in the mid-1980s.
 
• The Public interest Litigation is a litigation filed in a court of law, for the protection of “Public Interest”, such as Pollution, Terrorism, Road safety etc.
 
• It also functions as an effective instrument for changes in the society or social welfare.

questions.question: Which is the most discussed river in the Rig Veda?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Sindhu**__ is the most mentioned river and the most prominent river is __**Saraswati**__.
 
• Ganga mentioned - 1 time, the Yamuna mentioned -3 times and Krishna is - 0 times.
 
• From the given options **Sindhu **is the most mentioned river.
 
• The most prominent river in the Rig Veda is Saraswati.
 
• The Rig Veda mentions the Saraswati river as between the Yamuna to the East and river Sutlej to the west.
 
• The Rigveda is an ancient Indian collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns and is one of the oldest extant texts in any Indo-European language.

questions.question: Who had constructed the “Vijay Stambh” at Chittorgarh?
questions.solution:
• Vijay Stambh was constructed by Mewar king, Rana Kumbha, in 1448 to commemorate his victory over the combined armies of Malwa & Gujarat led by Mahmud Khilji.
 
• Vijay Stambh is located in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan.

questions.question: Who is credited with introducing the Dravidian style of architecture and sculpture in the South Indian Peninsula?
questions.solution:
• Pallavas were the ones who introduced the Dravidian style of architecture and sculpture in the South Indian Peninsula.
 
• Dravidian architecture comprised of pyramid shaped structures and temples created of sandstone, soapstone or granite.
 
• Dravidian architecture had three major elements - Porches that cover the entrance, Gate-pyramids, and Pillared halls.

questions.question: To which of the following options is the Sufi sect originally related?
questions.solution: Sufism arose from within Islam in the 8th-9th centuries C.E. as an ascetic movement.Practitioners of Sufism have been referred to as "Sufis".

questions.question: On the bank of which river is Budapest located?
questions.solution:
• The Budapest is located on the banks of Danube river.
 
• Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.
 
• The Danube is Europe's second longest river, after the Volga and flows through 10 countries.

questions.question: What is the main source of irrigation in Punjab and Haryana?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The main source of irrigation in Punjab and Haryana is **Canal**__.
 
• Canals are second most important source of irrigation in India after wells and tube wells.
 
• Canals are an effective source of irrigation in areas of low level relief, deep fertile soils and perrenial source of water.

questions.question: Which of the following countries has “Durand Line” as their international boundary?
questions.solution:
• The Durand Line is the 2,430-kilometre long international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• It was established in 1896 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Abdur Rahman Khan.

questions.question: From which of the following options is the Deccan Trap in Western India mainly formed?

options.text: Volcanic rocks like Basalt, Lava flow etc.
Fragmentary rocks like sand, pebbles etc.
Plutonic rocks like Granite, Graebo, Daiorite etc.

questions.solution:
• The Deccan Trap in Western India is mainly formed from Volcanic rocks like Basalt, Lava flow etc.
 
• The Deccan Trap in Western India are one of the largest volcanic features on Earth.
 
• The Deccan Traps are famous for the beds of fossils.

questions.question: In photosynthesis which gas is released by the green plants?
questions.solution:
• Plants release Oxygen during the process of photosynthesis.
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which plants make their food using light energy to make sugars from CO₂ and H₂O.
 
• Oxygen is given off as a by-product of photosynthesis.

questions.question: In which of the following is the speed of sound faster?
questions.solution:
• The speed of sound is faster in solid materials, slower in liquids and slowest in gases.
 
• It is easier for sound waves to go through solids than through liquids because the molecules are closer together and more tightly bonded in solids.

questions.question: Which of the following is measured with the help of “manometer” instrument?
questions.solution: A Manometer is a device which is used to measure pressure.A common simple manometer consists of a U shaped tube of glass filled with some liquid.

questions.question: The freely suspended magnetic needle always points in which direction?
questions.solution:
• The freely suspended magnetic needle always points in the North-South direction because of the presence of Earth's magnetic field.
 
• When a magnet is suspended freely, the north pole of the magnet gets attracted towards the geographical north and the south pole of the magnet gets attracted towards the geographical south.

questions.question: Why is the flash of lighting seen earlier than the sound of thunder?

options.text: Thunder is more near than roaring
The light can pass though vacuum
Speed of light is more than speed of sound
Speed of sound is more than speed of the light

questions.solution:
__
 
• The flash of lighting is seen earlier than the sound of thunder because the** speed of light is more than speed of sound.**__
 
• Light at a speed of around 300,000,000 meters per second travels much faster than sound which moves at 340 meters per second.
 
• A person 1 km away from the thunderstorm hears the thunder about 3 seconds after seeing the lightning flash.

questions.question: Computer’s ‘IC’ chips are usually made of which of the following?
questions.solution:
• Computer’s ‘IC’ chips are usually made of Silicon because it is a semiconductor i.e. it conducts electricity under some conditions and acts as an insulator under others.
 
• Silicon’s electrical properties can be modified through a process called doping which makes it an ideal material for IC chips.

questions.question: Water that does not make foam quickly with soap is ______.
questions.solution:
• Hard water does not make foam quickly with soap.
 
• Soap is less effective in hard water because it contains high concentration of dissolved minerals like calcium ions and magnesium ions in the form of dissolved salts.

questions.question: Which acid is used in car battery?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Sulphuric Acid**__ also is known as "Battery acid" is used in the car battery.
 
• A mixture of sulfuric acid and water is used as the electrolyte in a lead-acid battery.
 
• Sulfuric acid is also used to make fertilisers, chemicals, paints, explosives, detergents.

questions.question: Electroplating does not help ______.

options.text: In protecting the metal against corrosion
In giving fine finish to the surface

questions.solution:
• Electroplating is the process of plating one metal onto another by hydrolysis to prevent corrosion of a metal.
 
• Electroplating is also used in providing a fine finish and shining appearance to the surface.
 
• This process does not help in making the metal hard because it creates just a fine layer of electroplating metal on the provided metal like iron.
 
• Metals commonly used in electroplating include zinc, copper and tin.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The number of replaceable hydrogen atoms of an acid is called its basicity
An acid must contain at least one hydrogen atom
Some acids contain more than 20 hydrogen atoms

questions.solution:
• **Basicity** - defined as the **no of ionizable hydrogen (H+) ions** present in one molecule of an acid
 
• By definition**, Bronsted-Lowry acids** must have a proton, so they must have hydrogen as **acids are a proton donor**
 
• **Some acids contain more than 20 hydrogen atoms** like **Oleic acid (C₁₈H₃₄O₂)** which has **34** hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Which Gas was leaked during Bhopal Gas Tragedy?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Methyl Isocyanate**__ was leaked during the Bhopal Gas Tragedy on the night of 2–3 December 1984 at the Union Carbide India pesticide plant in Bhopal.
 
• Methyl Isocyanate is used in the production of rubbers and adhesives.
 
• It is a colorless, poisonous, irritating material and is extremely hazardous to human health.

questions.question: Which is the most hazardous metal pollutant of automobile exhaust?
questions.solution:
• The Most hazardous metal pollutant of the automobile exhaust is Lead.
 
• Lead is a highly toxic metal whose widespread use has caused extensive environmental contamination and health problems.
 
• Lead is hazardous as it can get into the food chain and cause heart disease.

questions.question: India has Kalapani and Susta territorial dispute with which of the following country?
questions.solution:
• India has Kalapani and Susta territorial dispute with Nepal.
 
• Kalapani is an area under territorial dispute in Darchula District of Nepal and Pithoragarh district of India which has been administered by India's Indo-Tibetan Border Police since the 1962.
 
• Susta is an Indian Army controlled area which lies between Tribenisusta, Nepal and Nichaul, Uttar Pradesh, India.

questions.question: Under the Indus Water Treaty (IWT), India has been given the exclusive right over the rivers of ______.
questions.solution:
• The Indus Waters Treaty is a water-distribution treaty between India and Pakistan which was signed in 1960 after nine years of negotiations with the help of the World Bank.
 
• According to the treaty, control over the water flowing from Beas, Ravi and Sutlej were given to India while Pakistan was given the control over Indus, Chenab and Jhelum.
 
• The treaty was signed in Karachi by then Prime Minister of India Jawaharlal Nehru and then President of Pakistan Ayub Khan.
